_comment: Editor UI metadata for B-LEG. Overlaid onto the schema built from BLegConfig (a SosFadeConfig superset). UI ONLY — never touches a trade decision or the source hash. Click Scan Strategies after editing. Params not listed here fall back to their raw field names; the SOS Fade gate params (arm sources, FVG/entry, HTF, veto) are inherited from the SOS Fade bot and still matter because the B-LEG keeps the 'SOS Fade has priority' stand-down — see the SOS Fade strategy's own meta for their descriptions. Labels and descs are shared with strategies/tradingview/b_leg_strategy.pine the same way the SOS Fade meta is — label == the Pine input title, desc == its tooltip, changed in the same commit. COPY STYLE (2026-08-10, Aaron's call): every desc is SHORT and PLAIN — what the setting does, what each choice means, and the one fact that changes the decision. No measurement dumps, no trade counts, no R figures, no dates, no file references: the strategy detail page is for reading, and the evidence behind a default lives in this package's CLAUDE.md and its optimization doc. Same rule for `edge` and `steps`.
edge: The SOS Fade reversals whose pullback turned up late — the setups SOS Fade gives up on with no trade. Price often does come back to them.

steps.label: 01 · Break
steps.title: A reversal fires
steps.detail: Structure breaks and the level to watch is marked, even though the reversal itself has not traded yet.

steps.label: 02 · Runs on
steps.title: The pullback never comes
steps.detail: Price expands and breaks structure again before pulling back, so the normal reversal dies with no trade. That death is what starts this setup.

steps.label: 03 · Late
steps.title: The pullback arrives anyway
steps.detail: An order rests at the marked level for a few days. If price comes back to it, the order fills. If it never comes back, or runs too far the other way, the setup is dropped.

steps.label: 04 · Manage
steps.title: Let it run
steps.detail: The same machinery as the main bot: the first target moves the stop to breakeven, the second lifts it further, and the trailing stop takes the rest.

tldr.text: It looks for an SOS Fade reversal that never got its pullback: price broke structure again the same way before retracing halfway.
It rests a limit order at the halfway point of that first break and waits up to {bleg_max_days} trading days for price to come back.
The stop sits at the start of that break. The first target is its far end; the second is the move's furthest point.
Nothing is banked early: the stop moves to breakeven at the first target, then trails behind the swings.
A trade short of its first target after {exec_time_stop_hrs} hours is closed. A close back past the break's start drops the setup.
It stands aside where SOS Fade would trade that side itself, skips the last hour before the daily close, and takes each setup once.
Each trade risks {exec_risk_pct}% of the account, one at a time. Unlike SOS Fade, it never adds to a winner or re-enters.

params.name: bleg_max_days
params.label: Days to watch for the late retrace
params.desc: How long the order waits for the late pullback before the setup is dropped. Counted in bars, so weekends and the daily close do not use it up.
guide: Only quick pullbacks fill
Waits longer for a late return — 4 to 5 days tested best

params.name: exec_tp1_level
params.label: Target 1 level
params.desc: Which fib the first target sits on. Auto = the shipped rule: a deep entry aims at 0.5, a shallow one at 0.382. Naming a level pins it for every trade. A level behind the entry is not a target, and that trade keeps the Auto level.
guide: Nearer target, hit more often
Further target, hit less often

params.name: exec_tp2_level
params.label: Target 2 level
params.desc: Which fib the second target sits on. Auto = a deep entry aims at 0.382, a shallow one at the swing extreme.
guide: Nearer target, hit more often
Further target, hit less often

params.name: exec_tp1_r
params.label: First target, in R
params.desc: Where the first target sits, measured in multiples of what the trade is risking. -1 = off, and the target stays on the level the setup gives it. 1 = one times the risk, on every trade.
guide: Bank nearer the entry, more often
Bank further out, less often

params.name: exec_risk_pct
params.label: Risk % per trade
params.desc: How much of the account each trade risks. The stop distance sets the position size, so a tighter stop buys a bigger position at the same risk.

params.name: exec_longs
params.label: Trade longs
params.desc: Lets long setups trade. Off = shorts only.

params.name: exec_shorts
params.label: Trade shorts
params.desc: Lets short setups trade. Off = longs only.

params.name: exec_no_late_day
params.label: No entries in the final hour (16:00-17:00 NY)
params.desc: On = no new entries in the last hour before the daily close, so a trade cannot be gapped out over the break.

params.name: exec_entry_block_from
params.label: No new entries from (New York, HH:MM)
params.desc: A part of the New York day in which no new trade may start — first entries and re-entries alike. 24-hour time, e.g. 11:30. Leave both times empty for off. It checks when the order would actually be live, so an order decided just before the window cannot fill inside it. Measured before it was built: 11:30-15:30 was 45 trades for +6.8R, so it is not a losing block to begin with.

params.name: exec_entry_block_to
params.label: ...until (New York, HH:MM)
params.desc: The end of the no-entry window, 24-hour time. The window may run past midnight (22:00 to 02:00). Must be set together with the start.

params.name: exec_runner_trail
params.label: Runner trail method
params.desc: How the stop follows the trade once the second target is hit. Fixed step is a plain dollar grid; structure parks it at the last swing.
guide: Fixed step — simplest, and the worst of the three
Structure + ratchet — best on the main bot, untested here

params.name: exec_struct_trail_buf_tk
params.label: Structure trail buffer (ticks)
params.desc: How many ticks beyond the last swing the trailing stop sits, so a wick through it does not clip you.
guide: Tight to the swing — clipped by wicks
Wide of the swing — survives noise, gives back more

params.name: exec_trail_pct
params.label: Runner ratchet step (% of price)
params.desc: How big each trailing step is, as a percent of price. Keep it small here - these trades risk very little of the price.
guide: Tighter — banks more of each run on this setup
Too big and the stop never moves at all here

params.name: exec_trail_step
params.label: Runner trail step ($ of price)
params.desc: The step size in dollars. On gold 1 pip is 10 cents, so 50 pips = 5.0.
guide: Tighter trail — banks sooner, cuts runners short
Looser trail — lets winners breathe, gives back more

params.name: exec_tp2_stop_mode
params.label: TP2 → stop floor
params.desc: Where the stop jumps to the moment the second target is hit. TP1 is tight and can scratch the trade; breakeven gives it the most room.
guide: TP1 price — protects the gain, scratches runners
Breakeven — maximum room for the runner

params.name: exec_time_stop_mode
params.label: Time stop
params.desc: Closes a trade that has been open longer than the hours set below. Before TP1 only cuts trades that never reached the first target.
guide: Off — the clock never closes a trade
Always — the clock closes winners too

params.name: exec_time_stop_hrs
params.label: Time stop (hours)
params.desc: How long a trade may stay open, in hours, weekends included.
guide: Cuts winners as well as losers
Fires on almost nothing

params.name: exec_aplus
params.label: SOS Fade has priority (stand the B-leg down)

options.on: SOS Fade stands the B leg down

params.desc: On = stand down on any side where the main reversal setup would have armed, which keeps results comparable with the parent. Off = every setup trades on its own.

params.name: flat_mode
params.label: Flat before the close
params.desc: Closes any open trade shortly before the market shuts, so nothing is held through a break. Friday only covers the weekend and the holiday closes of the same shape; Every day also closes overnight. Off by default.

params.name: flat_holidays
params.label: ↳ Also flatten before holiday closes
params.desc: Covers the early closes and market holidays too — Christmas Eve, New Year's Eve, the Thursday before Good Friday and Thanksgiving. Read only when Flat before the close is on.

params.name: exec_giveback_arm_r
params.label: Give-back guard: arm at (R)
params.desc: Watches how much of its best price a trade hands back. -1 switches it off and nothing changes. Any other number is how far in front the trade must have been, in R, before the guard starts watching. It reads the trade's own best price, not a target, so a trade that never gets that far is managed exactly as it is today.
guide: Low — protects small winners, and costs the big ones far more than it saves
Off at -1, or high — only the trades that were well in front are watched

params.name: exec_giveback_pct
params.label: How much of the best it may hand back (%)
params.desc: Read only when the guard is armed. 50 means the guard fires once the trade has given back more than half of its best. MEASURED: tighter is worse, not better — a quarter and a third both score below half, because a trade that cannot breathe is stopped out of the move it was right about.
guide: Tight — fires often, and cuts trades that were only pausing
Loose — fires almost never

params.name: exec_giveback_action
params.label: What it does when it fires
params.desc: Read only when the guard is armed. Close flattens the trade at the next bar's open. Tighten the stop leaves it open and puts it straight on the runner trail. Bank half sells half of what is still open and puts the rest on that trail, and fires once per trade. MEASURED over 2020-2026: tightening kept 11R more than closing for the same drawdown.
guide: Close — takes the money and gives up the rest of the move
Hand to the trail — keeps the runner, gives back a little more

params.name: exec_rev_exit
params.label: Reversal exit: what it does
params.desc: Watches for a shift of structure against an open trade on the FASTER chart — the same 5-minute stream the re-entry fills on — and acts on it. Off changes nothing. This is a SIGNAL rather than a percentage: the give-back guard above fires off the trade's own profit curve, which says nothing about whether the market turned, while this fires off what the market actually did. It reads the faster chart because a 15-minute reversal is confirmed long after the turn, by which time the profit is already gone. It only ever touches the first trade of a setup, never a re-entry.
guide: Off — the trailing stop is the only thing protecting an open profit
On — a turn on the faster chart can bank or protect what the trade showed

params.name: exec_rev_arm_r
params.label: Arm once the best has reached (R)
params.desc: Read only when the reversal exit is on. How far in front the trade must have been, in R, before a turn against it can close anything. Without it this would be a second stop loss: a trade that has never been in profit already has a stop, and the stop is the faster of the two. The guard exists for the trade that showed real money and handed it back.
guide: Low — watches almost every trade, including ones only pausing
High — only the trades that were well in front are watched

params.name: exec_rev_trigger
params.label: What counts as a reversal
params.desc: Read only when the reversal exit is on. Structure shift: structure turns against the trade on the 5-minute chart (measured: lost on every setting). Level rejected: price reaches the same major level ahead of the trade — a weekly, daily or 4-hour high or low — and fails to close through it on separate visits. Support holding behind the trade never counts. Measured: this one lost on every setting too.

params.name: exec_rev_level_touches
params.label: Rejections of the same level before it acts
params.desc: Read only when the trigger is Level rejected. 2 means it acts on the second failed visit. Bars pressing against the level one after another count as one visit.
